To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a thin compositionally-graded n+/ν/ρ/p HgCdTephotodiode is shown to be a viable option for high temperature operation.
the optical and electrical performance can be enhanced by reducing the volume of the active layer and increasing the quantum efficiency.
we show the feasibility of operation of a HgCdTe IR FPA at elevated temperature by reducing the active volume of the detector and by employing the band filling effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new architecture of infrared detector for high temperature operation.
the development of a high-performance, high-resolution, and low-cost infrared imaging system for elevated operation temperatures.
the development of a novel architecture of HgCdTE infrared detector for elevated operation temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reported design would be suitable for the operation of the infrared FPA up to 160K.
the proposed design is capable of meeting the NETD requirement of 20 mK or less at 160 K.
the reported design is a significant improvement over the current state-of-the-art HgCdTe FPA for elevated temperature operation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed design is capable of operating the HgCdTe infrared FPA at elevated temperature with reduced volume and reduced power consumption.
the HgCdTe FPA can be operated at elevated temperature without compromising the NETD and the ROIC can be designed with smaller charge handling capacity.
the proposed HgCdTe FPA architecture can be operated at 160 K and still provide the desired performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to operate the HgCdTe infrared FPAs at elevated temperatures without compromising the NETD performance by reducing the volume of the absorber layer and hence, reducing the charge handling requirement in the ROIC.
the HgCdTe FPAs with the proposed design will be more robust at elevated temperatures.
a thin HgCdTe device can be operated at high temperature with high quantum efficiency and low dark current.
